data.name: Aaeesha
data.gender_notes: Aaeesha is used as a unisex name in islamic naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Living; alive; she who lives (the name of the Prophet's wife ʿĀʾiša)
data.long_meaning: From Arabic ʿāʾiša (عائشة) 'living, alive', the feminine active participle of ʿāša 'to live', from the root ʿ-y-sh. It is the name of ʿĀʾiša bint Abī Bakr, a wife of the Prophet Muhammad and a major narrator of hadith. Aaeesha therefore means “Living; alive; she who lives (the name of the Prophet's wife ʿĀʾiša)”. Arabic feminine name ʿĀʾiša 'living, alive'; borne by ʿĀʾiša bint Abī Bakr, a wife of the Prophet and a major hadith narrator.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aaeesha expresses “Lady of the house, or the one who is free from sin”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From Arabic ʿāʾiša (عائشة) 'living, alive', the feminine active participle of ʿāša 'to live', from the root ʿ-y-sh. It is the name of ʿĀʾiša bint Abī Bakr, a wife of the Prophet Muhammad and a major narrator of hadith.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aaeesha total 22, reducing to 4. Number 4 is associated with discipline, order and steady effort.

faq.q: Who was ʿĀʾiša in Islamic history?
faq.a: ʿĀʾiša bint Abī Bakr was a wife of the Prophet Muhammad and one of the most important narrators of hadith. The name Aaeesha is the same Arabic name عائشة, meaning 'living, alive'.

faq.q: What does the name Aaeesha mean?
faq.a: Aaeesha means “Living; alive; she who lives (the name of the Prophet's wife ʿĀʾiša)”.

faq.q: Where does the name Aaeesha come from?
What is the linguistic root of Aaeesha?
faq.a: The root of Aaeesha is ع-ي-ش (ʿ-y-sh).

faq.q: How is Aaeesha written in Arabic script?
faq.a: Aaeesha is written عائشة in Arabic script.

faq.q: Is Aaeesha a boy's or a girl's name?
faq.a: Aaeesha is used as a female name.

faq.q: Does Aaeesha appear in the Qur'an?
faq.a: No. Aaeesha is not a Qur'anic name; it is used in Muslim naming tradition.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Aaeesha verified?
faq.a: Yes — the meaning “Living; alive; she who lives (the name of the Prophet's wife ʿĀʾiša)” is established by Arabic feminine name ʿĀʾiša 'living, alive'; borne by ʿĀʾiša bint Abī Bakr, a wife of the Prophet and a major hadith narrator..
